The test image shows soybean leaves with prominent interveinal chlorosis — yellowing between the veins while the major veins appear to remain green. There are also some small reddish-brown spots. This pattern is classic for Sudden Death Syndrome or Brown Stem Rot.

Let me check the reference image for Sudden_death_syndrome.

The reference image for Sudden Death Syndrome (top-right panel) shows exactly the same pattern as the test image: interveinal chlorosis with the major veins remaining green, creating a mottled yellow-green appearance on the leaf. This matches perfectly.

The test image shows:
- Yellowing/chlorosis between leaf veins
- Major veins and midvein remaining green
- Large chlorotic blotches developing between veins
- Leaves still attached (petioles remain on stem)

This is a textbook presentation of Sudden Death Syndrome.
